candidate_name: Syrian LNG import (Banias / Latakia FSRU) — NOT confirmed as a discrete project
sponsor_or_proposer: None identified for a Syria-sited terminal. Post-Assad gas supply to Syria is being delivered via Qatar (financed by Qatar Fund for Development) and routed through JORDAN's Aqaba terminal, not a Syrian port.
current_state: No Syrian LNG import terminal exists or is concretely proposed. Following Assad's fall (Dec 2024), Qatar began financing LNG imports (from ~March 2025) to power Syria's Deir Ali plant (~400 MW), but the LNG is regasified at Jordan's Aqaba FSRU and piped north via the Arab Gas Pipeline (with US sanctions clearance). The brief's hypothesized 'Banias FSRU' was not substantiated — sources explicitly route the arrangement through Aqaba rather than Syrian ports (Banias/Latakia).
missing_threshold_elements: No sponsor for a Syria-sited terminal; no approximate Syrian terminal location committed; no concrete step (no FSRU charter, tender, or siting decision) for a terminal physically in Syria. Fails all three add-bar elements.
watch_for: A dedicated Syrian-coast FSRU or onshore regas proposal (Banias, Latakia, or Tartus) with a named sponsor/charterer; any pivot of the Qatar/Jordan-routed supply into a Syria-sited import terminal; reconstruction-era MoUs naming a Syrian LNG receiving facility.
notes: Confirms Syria correctly has 0 GEM LNG-terminal rows; the cross-border supply belongs to Jordan's Aqaba record, not a new Syrian terminal. No new_terminal warranted this batch. Re-check next batch as Syrian energy reconstruction is fast-moving.
